problem: The superscripts and subscripts are missing in the body text, so the formulas read as μ′r=E[Xr], μ′r=Σ xrp(x) and μr=Σ (x−μ)rp(x). A student can read 'Xr' as X times r, and 'μ′r' as μ′ times r, which is wrong.
fix: Write them with the inline tags: μ′<sub>r</sub> = E[X<sup>r</sup>], μ<sub>r</sub> = E[(X−μ)<sup>r</sup>], Σ x<sup>r</sup> p(x) and Σ (x−μ)<sup>r</sup> p(x).

where: Section 3, last paragraph before the figure
problem: 'The same absolute-convergence caution applies when r is large' suggests convergence is only a worry for high r. In fact each moment needs its own convergence check for every r, and a high moment can fail even when low ones exist (a heavy-tailed distribution may have a mean but no variance).
fix: Say: the moment E[X<sup>r</sup>] exists only if Σ |x|<sup>r</sup> p(x) (or ∫ |x|<sup>r</sup> f(x) dx) is finite; this check is needed for every r, and higher moments can fail even when lower ones exist.
